claim_verdicts.evidence: servers/index.md (moniker >= 2.2): "Kestrel server is the default, cross-platform HTTP server implementation." kestrel.md, moniker ">= aspnetcore-10.0": "Kestrel is the recommended server for ASP.NET Core, and it's configured by default in ASP.NET Core project templates" and "ASP.NET Core project templates use Kestrel by default when not hosted with IIS." Both halves of the claim (default server; the one templates configure) are stated for 10.0. The round-1 blocker wording ("every ASP.NET Core app runs on") is gone.

servers/index.md: "An ASP.NET Core app runs with an in-process HTTP server implementation. The server implementation listens for HTTP requests and surfaces them to the app as a set of request features composed into an HttpContext." kestrel/endpoints.md on transport: "The code binds together TCP-based HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 with QUIC-based HTTP/3"; "The address is usually a TCP address and port number." The new scoping ("a TCP connection for the HTTP/1.1 traffic in this course") is exactly what the docs support; the round-1 HTTP/3-over-QUIC objection is answered.

servers/index.md: the server "listens for HTTP requests and surfaces them to the app as a set of request features composed into an HttpContext" — it produces request objects for other code. fundamentals/routing.md L20: "Routing is responsible for matching incoming HTTP requests and dispatching those requests to the app's executable endpoints. Endpoints are the app's units of executable request-handling code. Endpoints are defined in the app and configured when the app starts." Path matching is app-side routing, not the server.

Body and status are literal tokens, no placeholders. claim_verdicts.evidence: Caddyfile@stage-0 L18-21: @getOrder is {method GET; path /api/v1/orders/1}; L41-44 respond `{"id":1,"customer_id":1,"status":"paid"}` 200 — a literal string. methods.txt shows the identical body returned for two consecutive GETs: {"id":1,"customer_id":1,"status":"paid"} twice, and "GET    /api/v1/orders/1  -> 200".

Caddy docs, respond directive: syntax "respond [<matcher>] <status>|<body> [<status>]" where "<body> is the response body to write." The two bodies in the quoted block are backtick-quoted literals with no {placeholder}, so the bytes written are the bytes in the file; methods.txt confirms an identical body on repeated GETs. The rewrite now scopes the claim to these two bodies ("Both bodies here are literal strings typed into Caddyfile") instead of asserting respond always sends a fixed body — round-1 minor resolved.

outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/methods.txt, captured at the tag, contains "Location: /api/v1/orders/13". The value cannot vary between runs: Caddyfile L38 is header Location "/api/v1/orders/13", a constant with no placeholder, and scripts/http/methods.sh greps '^(HTTP/|Location:)' from a real POST. I did not start Docker to run the lab twice; the constant config plus the captured run settle determinism.

servers/index.md: "An ASP.NET Core app runs with an in-process HTTP server implementation." kestrel/when-to-use-a-reverse-proxy.md: "Kestrel can be used by itself or with a reverse proxy server. A reverse proxy server receives HTTP requests from the network and forwards them to Kestrel"; "When Kestrel is used as an edge server without a reverse proxy server, sharing of the same IP address and port among multiple processes is unsupported. When Kestrel is configured to listen on a port, Kestrel handles all traffic for that port." Distribution is a separate box in front.

kestrel/security-considerations.md (moniker >= 8.0, in force for 10.0): "Kestrel includes limits, timeouts, protocol validation, and middleware integration points that help reduce the impact of malformed traffic." Its 400 table lists parse failures Kestrel itself detects: "InvalidRequestLine, InvalidRequestHeader, InvalidRequestHeadersNoCRLF, InvalidRequestTarget, InvalidCharactersInHeaderName, InvalidContentLength... MissingHostHeader", plus "HTTP/1.1 requests without a Host header are rejected with 400 Bad Request."

Caddyfile@stage-0 L11-12 (:8080 { root * /srv/www) and L87-89 (handle { file_server }); docker-compose.yml mounts ./www:/srv/www:ro and www/index.html exists in the tag's tree. Caddy docs, file_server: "A static file server that supports real and virtual file systems. It forms file paths by appending the request's URI path to the site's root path." So index.html is read off disk; only the respond bodies live in Caddyfile. The round-1 major (sentence implied index.html came from Caddyfile) is fixed.

issues.quote: every request there today gets the same fixed JSON back from Caddy
issues.text: True only for POST. At stage-0 only @postOrder matches the bare path /api/v1/orders ({method POST; path /api/v1/orders}); @getOrder, @replaceOrder and @deleteOrder all match /api/v1/orders/1. A GET or PUT to /api/v1/orders falls through to the final `handle { file_server }` under `root * /srv/www` and gets a static-file 404, not JSON. A learner who curls that path with GET sees exactly what the sentence says cannot happen.
issues.fix: Write "every POST there today gets the same fixed JSON back from Caddy" (the Try it step already uses POST), or "the two order paths the lab answers today hand back fixed JSON".

issues.quote: The diagram shows the shape of every request an ASP.NET Core app answers, whatever the app does.
issues.text: The diagram's server participant is named Kestrel, so this reads as "Kestrel is in the path of every ASP.NET Core request" — the same over-generalisation that was removed from Core concepts in round 1. servers/index.md names IIS HTTP Server as the in-process server under IIS in-process hosting, and HTTP.sys as an alternative. The step shape is universal; the name Kestrel is not.
issues.fix: Change to "The diagram shows the shape of every request an ASP.NET Core app running on Kestrel answers, whatever the app does."

issues.quote: a program you wrote yourself that only reads the bytes off the connection chokes on a header a real browser sends
issues.text: A program that only reads and prints bytes cannot choke on a header — it prints whatever arrives. The observable failure is on the client side: nothing well-formed comes back, so the browser reports an error. Choking on a header is what happens once a program starts parsing (folded headers, oversized header blocks, chunked bodies), which is not what this sentence says the program does.
issues.fix: Rewrite the cue as: "You notice this when the browser reports an error against your own byte-printing program: it received the bytes, but nothing it sent back was a response a browser could read."

issues.quote: since nothing in the stack seems to call it
issues.text: The only meaning of `stack` I was ever taught is the memory region for local variables and calls. Here it means something else (the lab? the programs running it?), and the words around it — "seems to call it" — push me straight back to the call-stack meaning. I stopped and guessed.
issues.fix: Replace "since nothing in the stack seems to call it" with "since nothing running in the lab seems to call it".

issues.quote: Caddy plays the role Kestrel will play once Đơn Hàng has a real API
issues.text: "API" is never defined. I have only seen those letters inside the path `/api/v1/orders`, which does not tell me what "having a real API" is. This sentence is the bridge from the situation to the diagram, so I had to invent a meaning ("real C# code behind those paths") to keep reading.
issues.fix: Replace "once Đơn Hàng has a real API" with "once Đơn Hàng answers `/api/v1/orders` with C# code".

issues.quote: `handle @postOrder` is the part Caddy uses when the request is a POST to `/api/v1/orders`
issues.text: The block shows two `handle` blocks but the prose names only `@postOrder`. I had to assume `@getOrder` is the GET counterpart; the lines that would tell me (where these names are defined) are not in the excerpt.
issues.fix: After "is a POST to `/api/v1/orders`" add: "and `handle @getOrder` is the part it uses for `GET /api/v1/orders/1`".

issues.quote: the same way `www/index.html` is copied verbatim off disk
issues.text: Two places compare Caddy's fixed answer to sending a file from disk, but nothing in this lesson or the prerequisites showed Caddy serving files, and `www/index.html` is a name I have never seen. The comparison explains the unfamiliar with something even less familiar, so it adds nothing for me.
issues.fix: Shorten the third misconception to "\"Caddy runs your C# code for you.\"" and end the suggested answer at "...copied verbatim from the `Caddyfile` on every request."

issues.quote: the same start-line-then-headers-then-body shape an earlier lesson described
issues.text: The prerequisite taught me "first line"; here it is "start-line", and q5's explanation says "start line". I paused to check these are the same thing before trusting the sentence.
issues.fix: Use the prereq's wording: "the same first-line-then-headers-then-body shape", and "first line, headers, body" in q5's correct explanation.

issues.quote: the default web server for ASP.NET Core apps, the one project templates configure and the one Đơn Hàng will run on
issues.text: The Kestrel bullet is one sentence carrying four things — default server, templates, Đơn Hàng, bytes to request and back — plus a dash-aside about TCP and HTTP/1.1. I read it three times. "the one project templates configure" also drops in a fact I cannot use anywhere in the lesson.
issues.fix: Split the bullet into two sentences: first what Kestrel is (the default web server for ASP.NET Core apps, the one Đơn Hàng will run on), then what it does (connection bytes into a request object, your code's decision back into response bytes).

issues.quote: Both bodies here are literal strings typed into `Caddyfile`, so `respond` sends exactly that text back on every matching request.
issues.text: The paragraph after the code block does three jobs in a row: reading the Caddy lines, saying what a real POST and GET ought to do, and saying what changes once Kestrel and C# arrive. I had to re-read it to keep the three apart.
issues.fix: Start a new paragraph at "A real `POST /api/v1/orders` should create..." so that reading the block and arguing what should happen are separate paragraphs.

issues.quote: False, because Caddy refuses every POST request at this tag, long before any block runs.

issues.fix: In q2 option d, replace "at this tag" with "at stage-0".

issues.fix: Reword q5 c and d so they share no tail and need no new term, e.g. c: "A database connection to read orders from" and d: "A second machine to share its connections with"; update explanation d to match.
